howToRead: Navy racks run in rows of three, from the wearer’s right, which is the left side of this rack. The top row is short when the number of ribbons is not divisible by three.

A star or an oak leaf is not extra decoration. It counts awards. A silver star on the Good Conduct Medal replaces five gold stars. Two bronze stars on a campaign medal are campaign phases, not two more medals. The Navy E uses a letter instead of a star.
timelineLead: Rank, assignments and deployments share one axis. Below them, Places follows the same ordered sequence as the Map. A bar opens the explanation.
uniformsLead: Grouped by type, in the order worn within each group.
mapLead: Pins follow Sergio's place sequence in order. Each stop has one primary category: Commands (blue) are the six assigned commands; Instruction (purple) covers Great Lakes, Biloxi, San Diego, and Fort Bragg; Bases (green) are home bases, NAS, NS, annexes, U-Tapao, Shoalwater, Bliss, and Blanding; Field (orange) are FOBs, camps, theater sites, and exercises; Port visits (yellow) are ship port calls, homeport ship visits, and city port stops; Flight stops (teal) are transit hubs and flight legs, including Camp Arifjan. San Diego is the sole exception to mutual exclusivity: it is both Instruction and Command host (NCTS). Use the buttons above the map to show one category or any mix. When a filter is on, each place or assigned command appears once (first visit keeps the number). Full map keeps every numbered visit. Play walks the visible stops in that same order. A dashed ring means the location is approximate.
sourcesLead: Years, units, and campaign phases come from the shadowbox worksheet. Award counts, schools, and specialties come from the service record.
equipmentLead: Body armor, helmets, weapons, comms and crypto gear, vehicles, and ships and boats, grouped by type. The cards are stock photographs of that kind of gear. A photograph from his collection, when there is one, is in the sidebar. Credits are on the Sources page.
